title: Путин заявил о крупных победах в Украине: реальность совсем иная
content_c:
Российский диктатор Владимир Путин заявил, что с начала 2026 года армия РФ захватила около 6500 кв. км территории Украины и 310 населённых пунктов. Однако, согласно данным Института изучения войны (ISW), фактическое чистое продвижение российских войск за январь–сентябрь составило всего 144,51 кв. км — значительно меньше площади, озвученной Путиным. При этом в отдельные месяцы российская армия теряла больше территорий, чем захватывала.
16 октября во время посещения вспомогательного пункта управления Объединенной группировки российских войск, где Путин проводил совещание с военным командованием, он заявил, что под контролем Украины остаются чуть более 10% территории Донецкой Народной Республики и 16,5% Запорожской области.
«Луганская Народная Республика полностью находится под нашим контролем», — цитируют Путина пропагандистские СМИ.
По подсчётам ISW, в январе 2026 года Россия захватила 318,54 кв. км, в феврале — 122,73 кв. км, а в марте — 23,04 кв. км.
В апреле российская армия потеряла 116,01 кв. км, в мае — ещё 281,1 кв. км. В июне российские войска захватили 30,02 кв. км, в июле — 37,85 кв. км, а в августе — 90,25 кв. км.
В сентябре ситуация вновь изменилась: Россия потеряла 80,81 кв. км.
Таким образом, по итогам девяти месяцев чистый прирост территории, оккупированной российской армией, составил 144,51 кв. км.
В ISW считают, что заявления Путина о масштабах российского продвижения не соответствуют реальной ситуации на фронте и «напоминают галлюцинации».
Институт отмечает, что Кремль активизировал свои длительные усилия по ведению когнитивной войны, формируя преувеличенное представление об успехах армии и создавая выгодную Москве картину происходящего на поле боя.
В то же время незначительное продвижение российской армии сопровождается большими потерями.
По подсчётам Центра стратегических и международных исследований (CSIS), с начала полномасштабного вторжения в феврале 2022 года до июня 2026-го российские войска потеряли около 1,4 миллиона военнослужащих, из которых не менее 450 тысяч погибли.
В первой половине 2026 года ежемесячные потери, по оценкам аналитиков CSIS, составляли 30–34 тысячи человек, тогда как набор новых контрактников обеспечивал российской армии около 27 тысяч военнослужащих в месяц.
В сентябре, по данным высокопоставленного военного представителя НАТО, российская армия потеряла более 50 тысяч военнослужащих, из которых 28 тысяч погибли.

title: "Сільпо" відкрив дизайнерський супермаркет з космічною темою у Києві
content_c:
Мережа супермаркетів "Сільпо" відкрила новий дизайнерський супермаркет у Києві, Residental Complex Taryan Towers (Іоанна Павла ІІ, 12), повідомили у пресслужбі компанії.
Дизайн супермаркета натхненний темою космосу.
ТОВ "Сільпо-Фуд", яке розвиває мережу "Сільпо", створено на початку серпня 2016 року. Станом на червень 2026 року в мережі працювало 312 супермаркетів.

title: A thousand slogans echoed here - but it could be the end for iconic Delhi protest site
content_c:
A thousand slogans echoed here - but it could be the end for iconic Delhi protest site
- Published
What is the point of a protest?
To raise your voice against injustice? To draw attention to a cause? Or to make those in power uncomfortable enough to listen?
For more than three decades, Indians have tried to do all three in a narrow, tree-lined road near Jantar Mantar, an 18th Century astronomical obervatory in Delhi.
But that may now be coming to an end.
This week, Delhi Police said Jantar Mantar, located close to parliament, would no longer be a designated protest site.
The decision comes months after the Gen Z-led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) - not a political party but a collective which began as a joke - led a massive protest there demanding the resignation of federal education minister Dharmendra Pradhan. Tens of thousands turned up and Pradhan subsequently resigned.
Police barricaded Jantar Mantar soon afterwards, preventing further demonstrations. Last week, an attempt by CJP supporters to march there, this time demanding the resignation of India's election chief, ended in a police crackdown.
Protesters have now been directed to three other sites. Two are far from parliament, while the third, the sprawling Ramlila Ground, is often booked months in advance. Unlike Jantar Mantar, which is free, all three charge tens of thousands of rupees a day.
Delhi Police says, external it acted after the Supreme Court suggested identifying alternative sites with adequate infrastructure. But critics say the move could push protests beyond the reach of ordinary Indians, further from the seat of power and into venues many cannot afford.
Over the years, Jantar Mantar has witnessed everything from mass movements that shook governments to small, lonely demonstrations by people desperate to be heard. Farmers, students, grieving parents and ex-soldiers have gathered under its trees, holding placards and shouting slogans. Not every protest made headlines, but for many, it was a place to turn to when other doors had closed.
This week, when the BBC visited, those scenes seemed a distant memory.
Yellow barricades blocked both ends of the road, with hundreds of paramilitary personnel standing guard, batons in hand.
In a nearby lane, uniformed men sat in shops drinking tea or scrolling through their phones. At one of the few shops without policemen, the shopkeeper folded his hands and said he did not want to answer any questions.
Built by Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II in the 1720s, Jantar Mantar was once better known as a tourist attraction than a place where a thousand revolutions were imagined.
Its story as a protest site began in 1993, when the then-Congress government stopped allowing demonstrations at the Boat Club lawns opposite the old parliament.
Historian Harleen Kaur has traced how, from the 1960s onwards, successive governments brought in new rules that shifted the site of protest in Delhi further away from parliament.
"Jantar Mantar, situated 3km (1.86 miles) from the Parliament House, [allowed the government] to contain protesting crowds at some distance from the Parliament House and PM's residence," she wrote in a 2023 paper, external.
Yet, the road saw countless spirited protests over the years.
Rachna Dhingra, an activist with the Bhopal Group for Information and Action, an advocacy group for survivors of a 1984 gas leak disaster, camped at Jantar Mantar with hundreds of others for around five months in 2008, trying to get the government to agree to demands including setting up a commission to allocate resources for rehabilitation schemes.
Through a scorching summer, they held press conferences, met politicians and even chained themselves to railings opposite then Prime Minister Manmohan Singh's residence to draw attention to their cause.
It was also where she formed solidarities with others - Tibetans protesting against China, activists opposing the displacement of people over large dam projects and even just lone protesters who caught a train from their home towns with nothing but a placard and a grievance.
"It can be lonely to protest but that place became a home for so many of us. We shared each other's stories, struggles and victories," says Dhingra.
Dipa Sinha, an academic associated with the Right to Food campaign, has seen ground-breaking laws - a landmark rural jobs guarantee scheme, the National Food Safety Act and Forest Rights Act - take shape at Jantar Mantar.
"It was a place where you could discuss issues with people who came to Delhi from across the country," she says.
Protesters would demonstrate outside government offices, including the erstwhile Planning Commission and the agriculture ministry, where they were often detained by police, before returning to Jantar Mantar to "gather, discuss and strategise".
But sustaining a protest for months was not easy.
Dhingra says they sheltered under tarpaulin sheets when it rained, used public toilets near the site and went to nearby gurdwaras to freshen up.
In 2017, the National Green Tribunal cited the lack of infrastructure, along with complaints from locals, to have Jantar Mantar shut down for protests.
A year later, the Supreme Court overturned this, citing the rights to free speech and peaceful assembly guaranteed under the constitution.
When asked whether the proximity to parliament made a difference to their cause, Dhingra quoted the reactions of her co-protesters who had come to Delhi for the first time.
"That's the president's house? Does the prime minister live there? How can they not listen to us when we are at their gates?" she remembered them saying.
Sinha points out that Jantar Mantar was also near institutions like the Press Club and Constitution Club, making it easier to get media coverage, and for politicians to drop by and meet protesters.
It was a simpler time - sometimes they would ask for permission from police only on the morning of the protest.
Those rules have become much stricter, external now.
In recent years, when Dhingra tried to protest at Jantar Mantar, she was told no-one could stay the night.
"Where do you go with hundreds of people who have travelled all the way to the capital to protest?" she asks.
While Jantar Mantar has its supporters, others share memories of an even more vibrant protest culture.
Mary E John, a gender studies scholar who lived in Delhi both as a student and as an academic, says that before 1993, she attended protests at the Boat Club on issues ranging from workers' rights and women's issues to topics of international significance.
"We lived in a climate where protest was part of life. In fact, we took it for granted," she says.
When the spacious Boat Club lawns made way for Jantar Mantar, it actually felt "claustrophobic", she said.
She pointed out that they, and others before and after them, protested at multiple sites - universities, colleges, streets - instead of just at Jantar Mantar.
She sees signs of that in protests by farmers who camped at Delhi's borders for months, and people who sat at the Shaheen Bagh neighbourhood demanding the repeal of a controversial citizenship law.
Even the 2012 anti-rape protests, she points out, were not restricted to Jantar Mantar but almost reached the Indian president's heavily guarded complex and beyond into other parts of Delhi.
It's not clear what Jantar Mantar's future is - the Supreme Court is hearing pleas challenging its removal as a protest site.
Opposition leader Rahul Gandhi and CJP leaders have said that Jantar Mantar belongs to the people and will be "reclaimed".
As the debate rages on, Jantar Mantar is the quietest it has been in decades - will it hear slogans again?

title: ‘Tough to watch, impossible to ignore’: reviewers on NAZA documentary
content_c:
Critics around the world have hailed the award-winning documentary NAZA as a “brilliant and harrowing” film that is “impossible to ignore”.
NAZA, which is produced by the Guardian and details Israel’s mass killing of civilians in Gaza, was released in UK cinemas this week and will be shown in more than 50 countries. As well as its global cinema releases, NAZA will be available free on the Guardian’s website from late November.
The investigative documentary, which contains 24 interviews with Israeli military insiders speaking anonymously on the rooftops of Tel Aviv at night, has received widespread praise.
In a five-star review, the Financial Times’s Danny Leigh says that as a piece of cinema, “journalism and film-making brilliantly entwine”. The Times calls the film “hugely provocative and a disturbing account” of Israel’s mass killing of civilians in Gaza, and the Irish Times brands NAZA an “essential record of engineered nightmare”. In a four-star review, the Guardian’s Peter Bradshaw says the “anguish of Gaza is brought into pin-sharp focus”.
British Vogue calls NAZA a “brilliant and harrowing film” that outlines the “restrained, meticulous, bone-chilling depiction of the progressive erasure of Gaza”. The magazine says the film “feels destined to become an enduring historical document, one which will and should be seen by generations to come”.
Time Out magazine says NAZA “puts together a restrained, intelligent, articulate, precise and utterly damning case against Israel’s actions in Gaza and their ongoing actions through the region. As a work of cinema, it is exemplary. As a work of journalism, it is inarguable. As a document, it is an indictment.”
The New York Times makes the film a “critic’s choice” and calls NAZA a “haunting” documentary that is “tough to watch, and impossible to ignore”. The Los Angeles Times says NAZA is a “stone-cold frightening” film that “burns the conscience”. And in New York magazine, it is described as “one of the most important films of our time”.
The Hollywood Reporter praises NAZA as a “sober and thoroughly documented bombshell of an exposé” that “leaves one with a deadening feeling, as if humanity may have lost all hope”. The Toronto Star says “NAZA is heartbreaking but essential viewing, questioning the systems that cause and quantify civilian death in modern warfare”.
The Spanish outlet El Mundo hailed NAZA as “the film of our time, a superb, electrifying, and devastating documentary about the systematic model of annihilation of the Palestinian people” that ultimately “points the finger at us. At night, in silence.”
The French newspaper Le Monde says the film “has the effect of an uppercut that leaves the viewer stunned”, while the Danish culture magazine Soundvenue calls NAZA a “soul-crushing testimony to the genocide in Gaza” that is an “example of how the world increasingly seems like a dystopia”.
The United Arab Emirates’ state-owned newspaper the National calls NAZA a “sickeningly tough film to watch”, and an editorial in the Israeli-outlet Haaretz says the film is “trying to force Israelis to confront what they already know: that Israel’s conduct of the war in Gaza has left a black stain”.
When the film opened in Italy last month, it topped the charts. The Italian newspaper Corriere della Sera says NAZA lasts “only 80 minutes, but no more is needed: the ‘scientific’ coldness with which the interviewees reconstruct how they are destroying Gaza is something unforgettable”.
The film contains 24 interviews with Israeli military insiders who detail how an AI-assisted apparatus of mass surveillance was activated during the Gaza war, revealing the systems that were used to target Hamas operatives in the knowledge that large numbers of Palestinian civilians would also die.
Various organisations, including the UN, Amnesty International, B’Tselem and Physicians for Human Rights, the latter two of which are Israeli-based, have said Israel is committing genocide against Palestinians in Gaza.
The film premiered at the Venice film festival, where it was received a 25-minute standing ovation – a festival record. The documentary went on to win the special jury prize.

title: Italy cuts air traffic in half amid data transmission issue
content_c:
Italy cuts air traffic in half amid data transmission issue
October 16, 2026
Air travelers across Italy faced delays and cancellations on Friday because of a problem with the country's air traffic control systems.
The ENAV air traffic control authority ruled out foul play such as a cyberattack, and said it was forced to introduce temporary restrictions of the volume of flights after identifying a data transmission problem.
Major airports in cities like Rome and Milan warned of likely disruptions and advised passengers to check with their airlines.
What did authorities say about the problem?
ENAV said it first identified the issue overnight. It was forced to restrict the volume of flights at around 6 a.m. (0400 GMT/UTC) as the number of scheduled services increased.
"We would like to inform you that this morning we guaranteed the greatest possible number of departures, including intercontinental flights," ENAV said.
Shorter-distance services were more likely to be interrupted.
"Despite the anomalies encountered on the data transmission network, we are deploying all available resources to minimize disruption and restore full operations as soon as possible," ENAV said. "We confirm an operational capacity of 50% of total air traffic, ensuring maximum safety at all times, which remains the Company's top priority."
ENAV said it had ruled out the possibility of the disturbance being caused by "malicious acts."
Rome airports operator ADR warned passengers that "flight delays and cancellations may occur" and advised passengers to contact their airline if uncertain. Milan airports company SEA issued a similar notice.
Edited by: Natalie Muller

title: Wirtschaftsministerin Reiche für Direktzahlungen nach "Tankrabatt"
content_c:
Ministerin zu Entlastungen Reiche für Direktzahlungen nach "Tankrabatt"
Der "Tankrabatt" soll Autofahrer entlasten - aber was kommt danach? Wirtschaftsministerin Reiche spricht sich im ARD Interview der Woche für eine gezieltere Entlastung von Geringverdienern aus - und erhöht den Druck auf das Finanzministerium.
Nach ihrem Besuch in Saudi-Arabien blickt Bundeswirtschaftsministerin Katherina Reiche nach eigenen Angaben besorgt auf die wirtschaftlichen Folgen der Energiekrise. Die Öltransporte seien zwar wieder auf dem Niveau von vor dem Iran-Krieg, sagte die CDU-Politikerin im ARD Interview der Woche. Die Golfstaaten schafften es also, "trotz der De-facto-Schließung der Straße von Hormus mit Hilfe von amerikanischen Begleitschiffen, Öltanker rauszubekommen".
Das große Problem seien aber die Ölprodukte wie Diesel, Kerosin, Benzin oder chemische Vorprodukte. Diese seien nach wie vor sehr knapp: "Hier ist die Produktion und auch der Transport auf unter 20 Prozent des Vorkriegsniveaus. Und diese Mengen fehlen."
Energiemarkt bleibt angespannt
Die Engpässe wirkten sich unmittelbar auf die Preise in Deutschland aus, sagte Reiche weiter. Zugleich gefährdeten sie die wirtschaftliche Erholung. Zentrale Frage sei, wie hoch die Inflation durch höhere Energiepreise ausfalle. "Das ist etwas, was uns mit Sorge erfüllt", sagte die Ministerin.
Gezielte Entlastungen statt pauschaler "Tankrabatt"
Den "Tankrabatt" hält sie laut eigenen Worten weiterhin für "ordnungspolitisch fragwürdig". Das Instrument setze aus ihrer Sicht falsche Anreize und könne den Spritverbrauch erhöhen. Für die Zeit nach dem "Tankrabatt" plädiert Reiche für ein zielgerichteteres Vorgehen: "Hier ist der Direktzahlungsmechanismus, der über das Bundesamt für Steuern ausgeben werden kann, der richtige Hebel."
Vorteil wäre: "Jemand mit geringem Einkommen, der wenig zu versteuern hat, kann diesen Betrag voll für sich konsumieren und nutzen. Und jemand, der das nicht nötig hat, muss ihn halt, wenn er ihn beantragt hat, zurückzahlen." Reiche sieht darin einen gerechteren Ansatz.
Sie kritisierte, dass der Direktzahlungsmechanismus bislang noch nicht genutzt werden kann. Die CDU-Politikerin fordert, das SPD-geführte Bundesfinanzministerium hier nicht aus der Verantwortung zu lassen.
Zugleich brachte Reiche eine Änderung des EU-Rechts ins Gespräch, um eine Senkung der Mehrwertsteuer auf Benzin und Diesel zu ermöglichen. Eine Mehrheit dafür in Europa zu schaffen, erscheine ihr "im Bereich des Möglichen", da ganz Europa unter hohen Preisen leide. Das Thema solle im EU-Finanzministerrat besprochen werden.
Ministerin arbeitet an Spritpreisdeckel
Einem Spritpreisdeckel steht sie auch nach dem Beschluss der Koalition, einen solchen einzuführen, weiter skeptisch gegenüber. "Der Spritpreisdeckel würde unmittelbar ins Raffineriegeschäft einwirken."
Es stelle sich die Frage, wie stark die Raffinerien belastet werden könnten, ohne die Versorgungssicherheit zu gefährden. Man müsse "dies erstens mit der Branche besprechen. Zweitens mit den Bundesländern, wo die Raffinerien sind und die ein hohes Interesse daran haben, dass ihre lokalen Versorgungsstrukturen nicht gestört sind. Und wir müssen drittens dafür sorgen, dass nicht am Ende des Tages aus Deutschland raus Benzin exportiert wird und wir teureren Sprit und das auch noch knapper haben".
Für Ende Oktober habe sie "die gesamte Branche, die Gewerkschaften, die Bundesländer" eingeladen, um "Für und Wider abzuwägen und einen Korridor auszuloten, was geht"
Arbeitszeit flexibilisieren und erhöhen
Großen Handlungsbedarf sieht die Wirtschaftsministerin beim Thema Arbeitszeiten: "Der Acht-Stunden-Tag stammt von 1918." Neben der Flexibilisierung der Wochenarbeitszeit, sollte es künftig auch möglich sein, dass man "die Wochenarbeitszeit ganz grundsätzlich erhöhen darf".
Reiche verweist darauf, dass hierzu bereits Gespräche zwischen Tarifpartnern laufen würden, um "auch werksbezogen die Arbeitszeit insgesamt nach oben zu bringen, um einfach effizienter arbeiten zu können". Sie unterstreicht: "Es wird nicht ohne mehr Arbeitsstunden gehen." Aus der Autoindustrie höre sie, dass allein die Einführung einer 40-Stunden-Woche pro Werk "zu 20 Prozent Effizienzgewinn" führen könne.

title: На войне против России погиб известный экс-футболист "Динамо"
content_c:
На войне против России погиб бывший футболист "Динамо" Роман Максимюк.
Об этом в своих социальных сетях сообщила его жена.
Личность Максимюка удалось установить спустя длительный период по результатам экспертизы ДНК.
Максимюк, который являлся наводчиком Сичеславской воздушно-штурмовой бригады, в последний раз выходил на связь в начале 2025 года и считался пропавшим без вести на покровском направлении Донецкой области.
"Прошу помнить моего Рому. Он был не просто пропавшим без вести. Он был мужем, папой, сыном, другом. Человеком, которого любили и ждали", — говорится в сообщении Веры Максимюк.
52-летний Роман Максимюк известен по своим выступлениям за "Динамо", "Днепр", "Волынь", а также российский "Зенит".
В активе бывшего полузащитника пять матчей в составе национальной сборной Украины. Осенью 2022 года он добровольно вступил в ряды ВСУ.
Ранее сообщалось о том, что ВСУ ликвидировали бывшего украинского футболиста.

title: Pepco готує магазини у Києві, Тернополі та Чернівцях до відкриття у 2026 р
content_c:
Київ. 16 жовтня. ІНТЕРФАКС-УКРАЇНА 2026 року – Pepco, один із провідних європейських дискаунтерів, продовжує вихід на український ринок: відкриття нових магазинів у Києві, Тернополі та Чернівцях заплановано до кінця 2026 року, вже запущено україномовний сайт, повідомили у пресслужбі компанії агентству "Інтерфакс-Україна".
Уточнюється, що у межах пілотного етапу Pepco у Києві нові магазини відкриються в ТРЦ Respublika Park, Retroville та Dream Yellow.
Заплановані відкриття магазинів стануть черговим важливим етапом поступового розширення діяльності Pepco в Україні. Компанія бачить значний потенціал українського ринку.
Для підтримки виходу на ринок Pepco вже запустила локальний україномовний сайт, що дає споживачам можливість ознайомитися з брендом та його асортиментом ще до відкриття нових магазинів: https://pepco.ua/. На сайті представлені актуальні колекції одягу, товарів для дому та дитячих товарів Pepco разом із цінами, інформацією для підтримки клієнтів і мапою магазинів.
Окрім комерційної діяльності, Pepco усвідомлює важливість підтримки українських громад. У межах цього зобов'язання компанія співпрацює з благодійним фондом "Діти Героїв", який надає допомогу українським дітям, що втратили одного чи обох батьків через війну. Завдяки цій ініціативі під гаслом "Солідарність, що має значення" Pepco прагне зробити внесок у вагому довгострокову підтримку постраждалих родин.
У релізі підкреслюється, що Pepco і надалі підходитиме до роботи в Україні відповідально, зважаючи на умови на ринку та тісно співпрацюючи з місцевою командою. Компанія виважено і поступово розбудовує свою присутність на ринку, ставлячи у пріоритет потреби українських споживачів.
Pepco – один із провідних європейських дискаунтерів широкого профілю, з головним офісом у Познані. Працює з 1999 року, має понад 4 тис. магазинів у 19 країнах. Бренд входить до групи Pepco Group. Група Pepco котирується на Варшавській фондовій біржі (PCO).

Для підтримки виходу на ринок Pepco вже запустила локальний україномовний сайт, що дає споживачам можливість ознайомитися з брендом та його асортиментом ще до відкриття нових магазинів: https://pepco.ua/. На сайті представлені актуальні колекції одягу, товарів для дому та дитячих товарів Pepco разом із цінами, інформацією для підтримки клієнтів і мапою магазинів.
Окрім комерційної діяльності, Pepco усвідомлює важливість підтримки українських громад. У межах цього зобов'язання компанія співпрацює з благодійним фондом "Діти Героїв", який надає допомогу українським дітям, що втратили одного чи обох батьків через війну. Завдяки цій ініціативі під гаслом "Солідарність, що має значення" Pepco прагне зробити внесок у вагому довгострокову підтримку постраждалих родин.
У релізі підкреслюється, що Pepco і надалі підходитиме до роботи в Україні відповідально, зважаючи на умови на ринку та тісно співпрацюючи з місцевою командою. Компанія виважено і поступово розбудовує свою присутність на ринку, ставлячи у пріоритет потреби українських споживачів.
Pepco – один із провідних європейських дискаунтерів широкого профілю, з головним офісом у Познані. Працює з 1999 року, має понад 4 тис. магазинів у 19 країнах. Бренд входить до групи Pepco Group. Група Pepco котирується на Варшавській фондовій біржі (PCO).

title: What we learned from heated US midterm Senate debates
content_c:
What we learned from heated US midterm Senate debates
- Published
Candidates running for the US Senate in next month's midterm elections have taken to the debate stage over the past few weeks - with some heated exchanges and stinging personal attacks.
As the 3 November election approaches and parties fight for control of Congress, some clear themes have emerged, particularly within some of the hotly-contested Senate races.
Here's what you need to know.
1. Not all Republicans are standing behind Trump
Republicans running for office are facing the same question they have been asked in elections since 2016: how aligned are they with President Donald Trump?
Conservatives who have bucked the president in the past have generally not fared well with voters.
The president has seen low approval ratings in recent months, with polls suggesting voters are largely concerned with the cost of living and high fuel prices.
While some Republican candidates have remained in lockstep with Trump, a Reuters analysis indicated, external that two-thirds of candidates in competitive US House and Senate races have broken with the president in some way this election cycle.
Susan Collins, a Maine Republican running for her sixth term in the Senate who has repeatedly broken with Trump, is again putting clear distance between herself and the president.
"I voted with President Biden 91% of the time," Collins said during a debate last week.
"The fact is, this year alone, this Congress alone, I voted against President Trump 137 times," she said.
Collins is fighting a tighter Senate race than she expected against Democrat Troy Jackson, the former president of the Maine Senate. A New York Times/Siena University poll from mid-September suggests Collins could be ahead in that race by 3%, while others indicate Jackson is in the lead.
Elsewhere, some Republican candidates are choosing to separate themselves from the Trump administration's specific policy decisions, while expressing loyalty to Trump himself.
In Iowa, traditionally a Republican stronghold, Congresswoman Ashley Hinson is facing a tougher-than-expected challenge in her Senate race.
She is taking on Democrat Josh Turek, and some polls suggest he has a narrow lead.
Hinson has not gone as far as Maine's Collins in separating herself from Trump, but she has broken with the president on some policy points.
During a 13 October debate with Turek, Hinson was asked about the Trump administration striking a deal with Russia to import 300,000 tonnes to the US, followed by several other shipments.
The Republican candidate did not mince her words: "We need to lower gas prices in this country, we need to lower diesel prices, but I don't think we need to be making a deal with Russia to do it."
2. Personal attacks are a common theme
As they have debated in recent weeks, the candidates haven't held back on deploying pointed personal attacks against their opponents.
The race for the vacant Michigan Senate seat - between rivals Abdul El-Sayed, a Democrat, and Mike Rogers, a Republican - has seen its fair share.
Rogers, a Trump-backed former congressman, questioned during a debate whether anyone in his Muslim opponent's family might be on a "watchlist".
El-Sayed, who would be the first Muslim member of the US Senate, pushed back strongly.
He called the Republican "a sock puppet for the Trump administration" and said he was "weak, cowardly [and] won't stand up until his poll numbers drop".
On Thursday, a protester interrupted the Maine debate and Collins suggested the disrupter was associated with her opponent.
Jackson hit back at Collins: "Oh shut up, I don't even know that kid."
Further south in Georgia, more personal attacks were exchanged between incumbent Democratic Senator Jon Ossoff and congressman Mike Collins, a Trump-backed Republican.
What started as an exchange where Ossoff accused Collins of taking money out of Georgians' hands to give to data centre developers, quickly turned into a hurling of insults that included Ossoff calling Collins a "bigot" who has "hired half the Third Reich".
Incendiary posts on social media from Collins' son-in-law, David Alan Scheer II, have become a point of contention in the race.
In one post, Scheer blamed "Israel and Zionist Jews" for policies he said were intended to "undermine the white, Christian nature of America".
Collins defended himself by accusing Ossoff of "spewing" "craziness".
"I've condemned racism, antisemitism, hate; I don't care where the source is," the Republican said.
3. Some candidates are skipping debates entirely
There are 35 Senate seats up for grabs this November, but in 21 there are no debates scheduled among the main candidates, an ABC News analysis found.
One race's lack of debates has surprised many observers: the Texas contest between James Talarico, a Democratic state representative, and Ken Paxton, a Republican and former state attorney general.
Polls in the typically Republican state suggest that Talarico could be in reach of a surprise win. Should he succeed, he could help give Democrats control of the US Senate by flipping one of the four seats they need to create a majority.
Talarico has accepted four debate invitations from different news networks. Paxton has not accepted any of those invitations.
In July, Paxton's campaign spokesperson told media outlets he would debate Talarico. But since then, the campaign and Paxton have said little on the matter.
Trump, who backed Paxton in the Republican primaries, has urged the candidates to debate.
"One thing about not showing up is you lose the opportunity to make the case for yourself, and instead, what you do is you give your opponent the ability and the opportunity to make your case as negative as possible," Peter Trumbore, a political science professor at Oakland University, told the BBC's US partner CBS News last month.
Follow the twists and turns of Trump's second term with North America correspondent Anthony Zurcher's weekly US Politics Unspun newsletter. Readers in the UK can sign up here. Those outside the UK can sign up here.

  - Published5 days ago

title: India’s Cockroach Janta party leader arrested amid crackdown on protests
content_c:
The leader of the Cockroach Janta party (CJP) youth movement, Abhijeet Dipke, was detained by police on Friday and then later formally arrested as authorities cracked down on fresh anti-government protests in the Indian capital.
Dipke was detained before a planned Friday evening demonstration he had called in central Delhi, urging supporters of the movement to come out and hold up the Indian flag.
On Saturday local media reported he was arrested “to prevent a breach of the peace”, with broadcasters NDTV and India Today saying he would be called before a special executive magistrate later in the day.
The Cockroach movement initially emerged back in May as online satire, but has since grown into one of the most substantial challenges to the powerful Modi government over its 12-year rule.
Alongside student groups and opposition parties, its supporters have in the past month been out on the streets across India’s biggest cities calling for the resignation of the chief election commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, who is accused of overseeing a revision of India’s electoral rolls that allegedly favours the ruling Narendra Modi government with the deletion of 130m names. The election commission and Modi’s Bharatiya Janata party (BJP) deny the claims.
The authorities, particularly in Delhi, have met the recent protests with a draconian crackdown, including bans on public gatherings, the deployment of tens of thousands of police, and detentions of thousands last weekend.
Friday’s protest was called by Dipke after the arrest and jailing of two of his fellow CJP leaders, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka. They were sentenced to five days in jail this week for jumping police barricades and holding a brief protest – including waving the Indian flag – at a site recently restricted by police for demonstrations in Delhi.
At a press conference on Thursday, Dipke condemned the “repressive” attempts to silence the CJP movement and called on supporters to come out and show Narendra Modi “that we are not afraid”. He added: “If waving the Indian national flag lands you in jail, we are ready.”
Delhi police had once again taken extreme measures to try to prevent Friday’s demonstration, due to be held at a park in a busy commercial centre in the heart of Delhi, from going ahead. Police were deployed en masse to the area and a police notice was sent to Dipke instructing him to call off the protest. The Delhi local authority also shut down the park where the protest was due to take place.
When Dipke refused to call it off, police detained him en route, just as people began to assemble for the protest. In videos captured of his arrest, the CJP leader was seen holding an Indian flag aloft and saying: “I have not broken any law right now … how can you detain me?” as he was led away by dozens of police officers.
In a post after his detention, the CJP posted on social media: “This government is so scared of the youth waving national flag.”
Neha Bora, a student leader who has become a figurehead of the protests, was also detained on Friday as she began a march in the centre of the capital.
Despite Dipke’s detention, about 2,000 protesters still gathered and unfurled flags at the protest around Delhi’s Connaught Place. Among them was 23-year-old Sanna, who said the brutal police crackdown on peaceful protests over recent weeks demonstrated that India was “on a pathway to dictatorship under the Modi government”.
“We are only out here to peacefully hold up the Indian flag and they treat us as if we are criminals, not citizens exercising our democratic rights,” she said. “Gyanesh Kumar must resign, and no matter what the police do, detaining us or crushing our skulls, we still won’t stop protesting until he is gone.”
Smaller protests also took place in Mumbai, Bengaluru and Patna on Friday.
The BJP has claimed that the Cockroach movement and the political opposition alliance have been holding protests to cause “anarchy” in the country. “Their sole intention is to stage a coup in the country,” said the BJP’s national spokesperson, Sambit Patra.
The authorities have also gone to unusual lengths to punish figures who have been seen at the recent protests calling for Kumar’s resignation.
In Mumbai, the Bollywood actor Imran Khan was given a notice to leave the country after he was detained by police while attending a demonstration last weekend. Khan, who holds a US passport, was told to leave the country by the end of the month, an order he is now challenging in the courts.

title: Clashes erupt at Argentine student protests against President Milei's austerity policies
content_c:
Clashes erupt at Argentine student protests
October 16, 2026
Protesters took to the streets in Argentina's capital, Buenos Aires, to demonstrate against libertarian President Javier Milei's cost-cutting measures for education.
Thousands of students, university staff, trade unionists and opposition supporters crowded outside the parliament, demanding the implementation of a law to finance universities.
While the rally was largely peaceful, clashes also erupted, with reports of masked individuals throwing stones at police, injuring at least eight officers. Some 25 people were arrested, according to the country's National Security Ministry.
Reports said other protesters had tried to push those throwing stones back. Police used water cannons and tear gas to disperse the crowds.
Security Minister Alejandra Monteoliva said the protesters wanted to "sow chaos," posting on her X account that the right to protest is not "a right to exercise violence."
Milei vetoes law, refuses to release funding
This was the fifth protest over the Milei government's education spending to take place since Milei entered office in 2023.Such a demonstration also took place in May, in which organizers say some 1.5 million people took part.
Milei vetoed a law, passed by Congress in 2025, requiring the government to invest more money in public universities.
The University Funding Law says the state should increase employees' salaries in line with inflation dated to December 2023. It also calls for the restoration of student scholarships and more funding for universities' operations.
Congress subsequently overrode Milei's veto, and several court rulings have instructed the government to release the funds, but it has so far refused to do so.
According to Milei, who was elected after promising wide-ranging cost-cutting measures, justified his veto by saying "there is no money" for inflation-linked spending increases.
A government spokesperson said the law had been "suspended" due to the government's legal action against it.
The first half of 2026 saw public spending on universities fall by 41% in real terms, according to the Center for National Economic Research of the University of Buenos Aires.
Argentina's education system is considered to be among the best in South America. Study at public universities is free, drawing students from across the region.
Edited by: Natalie Muller

title: Sean »Diddy« Combs in anderes Gefängnis verlegt – offenbar wegen Prügelei
content_c:
Inhaftierter Musiker Sean »Diddy« Combs in anderes Gefängnis verlegt – offenbar wegen Prügelei
Der wegen Nötigung zur Prostitution verurteilte US-Rapper Sean Combs, 56, ist in ein kleineres Gefängnis verlegt worden. Hintergrund ist offenbar eine erneute Prügelei mit Mitgefangenen. Zudem gab es Berichte über einen verhältnismäßig luxuriösen Lebensstil hinter Gittern. NBC News zufolge habe er Zugang zu Handys und Alkohol gehabt und ließ andere Inhaftierte für ihn kochen und putzen. Er soll auch Massagen erhalten haben.
Zuvor hatten US-Medien berichtet, dass Combs nach einer Schlägerei mit einem anderen Insassen am Wochenende wegen einer Kopfverletzung im Krankenhaus behandelt werden musste. Im Juli war Combs Medienberichten zufolge bereits wegen eines ähnlichen Vorfalls in Einzelhaft verlegt worden.
Die Gefängnisbehörde bestätigte die Verlegung, sagte jedoch nichts über den Grund. Der 56-Jährige wurde aus der Haftanstalt Fort Dix in New Jersey ins Allenwood Low Gefängnis im benachbarten Bundesstaat Pennsylvania gebracht, wie eine Sprecherin der US-Strafvollzugsbehörde am Freitag der Nachrichtenagentur AFP mitteilte.
Bei beiden handelt es sich um Männergefängnisse einer niedrigen Sicherheitsstufe, doch sie unterscheiden sich deutlich in ihrer Größe. In Fort Dix sind rund 4000 Häftlinge untergebracht, in Allenwood Low nur etwa 1000.
Der frühere Rap-Superstar sitzt aktuell eine Gefängnisstrafe von vier Jahren und zwei Monaten ab. Der Prozess offenbarte das düstere Privatleben einer der einflussreichsten Persönlichkeiten der Musikszene. Zeugenaussagen berichteten von Gewalt, Drogen und sexuellen Aufführungen, die Combs angeblich »Freak-Offs« oder »Hotel Nights« nannte.

Im Juli vergangenen Jahres war Combs wegen des Transports von Menschen über Bundesstaatsgrenzen hinweg zum Zweck der Prostitution schuldig gesprochen worden. Von den schwersten Anklagepunkten wie Bildung einer kriminellen Vereinigung sprachen ihn die Geschworenen frei. Als Strafmaß wurden im Oktober 2025 50 Monate Haft sowie eine Strafzahlung von einer halben Million Dollar (rund 427.000 Euro) festgesetzt. Combs soll im März 2028 aus der Haft entlassen werden.

Zuvor hatten US-Medien berichtet, dass Combs nach einer Schlägerei mit einem anderen Insassen am Wochenende wegen einer Kopfverletzung im Krankenhaus behandelt werden musste. Im Juli war Combs Medienberichten zufolge bereits wegen eines ähnlichen Vorfalls in Einzelhaft verlegt worden.
Die Gefängnisbehörde bestätigte die Verlegung, sagte jedoch nichts über den Grund. Der 56-Jährige wurde aus der Haftanstalt Fort Dix in New Jersey ins Allenwood Low Gefängnis im benachbarten Bundesstaat Pennsylvania gebracht, wie eine Sprecherin der US-Strafvollzugsbehörde am Freitag der Nachrichtenagentur AFP mitteilte.
Bei beiden handelt es sich um Männergefängnisse einer niedrigen Sicherheitsstufe, doch sie unterscheiden sich deutlich in ihrer Größe. In Fort Dix sind rund 4000 Häftlinge untergebracht, in Allenwood Low nur etwa 1000.
Der frühere Rap-Superstar sitzt aktuell eine Gefängnisstrafe von vier Jahren und zwei Monaten ab. Der Prozess offenbarte das düstere Privatleben einer der einflussreichsten Persönlichkeiten der Musikszene. Zeugenaussagen berichteten von Gewalt, Drogen und sexuellen Aufführungen, die Combs angeblich »Freak-Offs« oder »Hotel Nights« nannte.

title: Schaltsekunde abgeschafft - kommt dafür die Schaltstunde?
content_c:
Generalkonferenz für Maß und Gewicht Die Schaltsekunde wird abgeschafft
Ein internationales Gremium hat festgelegt: Künftig wird es keine Schaltsekunden mehr geben. 27 Mal wurde sie genutzt, um unsere Uhren mit der astronomischen Zeit in Einklang zu halten. Ein neues System käme erst im Jahr 3000 zum Einsatz.
Die Erde eiert. Sie rotiert nicht komplett gleichmäßig, mal ist sie langsamer, mal schneller. Daran ist unter anderem der Mond schuld. Die Gezeitenkräfte, die auch für Ebbe und Flut sorgen, bremsen die Erde und machen so den Tag ständig etwas länger.
Zugleich sorgt das Abschmelzen von Gletscher und Polkappen dafür, dass sich die Rotation beschleunigt. Die verschiedenen Effekte sorgen dafür, dass die genaue Veränderung der Erdrotation nicht vorhergesehen werden kann.
Unterschied zwischen Sonnen- und Atomzeit
Der Unterschied zwischen der Sonnenzeit - also von einem Sonnenhöchststand bis zum nächsten - und der internationalen Atomzeit wurde deshalb bisher immer nach Bedarf angepasst. Zweimal im Jahr, Ende Juni und Ende Dezember, gab es die Möglichkeit, eine Schaltsekunde einzufügen. Nach 23:59:59 gab es dann eine zusätzliche Sekunde, 23:59:60, bevor die Uhr auf 0:00 Uhr sprang. Das letzte Mal gab es eine solche Schaltsekunde zum Jahreswechsel 2016/17. Seit Einführung 1972 waren es insgesamt 27 Schaltsekunden.
Probleme für Computersysteme
Das kann allerdings zu Problemen bei Computersystemen, in Datenbanken oder Netzwerken führen. Da es keine Regelmäßigkeit gibt, wann es zu einer Schaltsekunde kommt, müssen viele Systeme manuell darauf vorbereitet werden. In Zukunft könnte es mit den bisherigen Regeln auch eine negative Schaltsekunde geben - der Tag wäre dann eine Sekunde kürzer - worauf Computersysteme noch weniger vorbereitet sind.
Gleichzeitig spielt es laut Beschluss der Generalkonferenz für Maß und Gewicht (CGPM) im Alltag keine Rolle, ob die Weltzeit minimal von der astronomischen Zeit abweicht. Für einen großen Teil der Weltbevölkerung weicht die Uhrzeit in der lokalen Zeitzone sowieso schon um mehr als eine Stunde von der Sonnenzeit ab.
Deshalb wurde auf der CGPM jetzt beschlossen, dass die Abweichung der astronomischen und der koordinierten Weltzeit bis zu einer Stunde betragen darf, bevor die Weltzeit angepasst werden muss.
Kein Handlungsbedarf in den kommenden Jahrhunderten
Wie genau das aussehen würde, ist nicht Teil des Beschlusses. Möglich wäre dann eine ganze Schaltstunde. Oder Länder könnten nach Bedarf ihre Zeitzone anpassen, um die gemessene Zeit an den Sonnenstand anzugleichen. Das würde sich dann anfühlen, wie der Wechsel von Sommer- auf Winterzeit. So oder so, statt alle paar Jahre gibt es jetzt höchstens alle paar Jahrhunderte Handlungsbedarf. Die erste Anpassung dieser Art wird nach dem neuen System etwa im Jahr 3.000 notwendig werden.

title: Які продукти краще не вживати на сніданок
content_c:
Які продукти краще не вживати на сніданок
Солодка випічка, підсолоджені напої та перероблене м’ясо можуть негативно впливати на здоров’я печінки, особливо якщо регулярно з’являються в ранковому раціоні.
Звичні продукти для сніданку можуть негативно впливати на здоров’я печінки. Дієтологи розповіли, споживання яких страв варто обмежити в ранковому раціоні та чим їх замінити.
Про це пише clinicalnutrition.
Шкідливі продукти для сніданку
Солодка випічка (пончики, круасани, булочки з начинкою): містять багато рафінованих вуглеводів і доданого цукру за відсутності клітковини. Метааналізи показують, що високе споживання ультраоброблених продуктів збільшує відносний ризик появи жирової хвороби печінки на 42%.
Солодкі кавові напої та коктейлі (кава із сиропами, пакетовані соки, солодкий чай): містять ударну дозу цукру (наприклад, порція холодного моко — до 24 г цукру), що перевантажує обмін речовин і веде до ожиріння печінки.
Перероблене м’ясо (бекон, сосиски, шинка): багате на насичені жири та сіль (натрій), надлишок яких спричиняє запальні процеси та метаболічні порушення.
Нагадаємо, звичайний перекус може стати частиною раціону для підтримання здоров’я серця. Кардіологиня та дієтологиня назвали сім вдалих варіантів і пояснили, на що звертати увагу.

title: Фон дер Ляйен: ЕС предоставляет 80% внешней помощи Украине
content_c:
Европейский Союз покрывает основную часть внешних потребностей Украины, но на следующий год денег не хватает. Председатель Европейской комиссии Урсула фон дер Ляйен после саммита в Брюсселе подтвердила, что дефицит финансирования на 2027 год составляет около 70 млрд евро. Потребности 2026 года уже обеспечены. На долю ЕС и его государств-членов приходится 80% внешней помощи, однако срочно нужны и другие партнеры, сообщает The Guardian.
«Реальность проста: пока эта война продолжается, потребности Украины в финансировании будут и дальше расти», — заявила фон дер Ляйен. Она подчеркнула: «В настоящее время на Европейский Союз и его государства-члены приходится 80% внешней помощи Украине, и мы будем и впредь играть ведущую роль. Но нам срочно нужны и другие партнеры, которые могли бы присоединиться». Также она добавила: «Как и на протяжении всех этих пяти лет войны, никто не хочет мира больше, чем народ Украины, и наш долг — поддержать его».
Речь идет о потребности в финансировании, а не о принятом решении выделить эту сумму. Аналогичную цифру называл и президент Украины Владимир Зеленский: по его оценке, война в следующем году обойдется в 155 млрд евро, и Украине потребуется как минимум еще 70 млрд евро на оборону, вооружение и обеспечение устойчивости. Уже согласованный кредит ЕС для Украины на 2026–2027 годы составляет 90 млрд евро.
Президент Европейского совета Антониу Кошта подтвердил, что Украина остается одним из главных приоритетов Европы. «Наша решимость поддержать Украину и ее народ остается неизменной. Каждый реальный шаг к миру имеет значение, и мы поддерживаем все реальные усилия в этом направлении. К сожалению, действия России указывают на противоположное», — сказал он. По его словам, Москва усиливает гибридные кампании в Европе: «Мы наблюдаем акты саботажа и неоднократные нарушения воздушного пространства государств-членов».
Правительство Украины 15 октября сообщило, что выполнило все условия для получения внешнего финансирования в 2026 году. Теперь необходимо согласование со странами ЕС. На 2027 год, по словам премьер-министра Сергея Корецкого, для бюджета еще нужно привлечь 32,6 млрд долларов.
О том, как превратить замороженные российские активы в долгосрочный ресурс для Украины, в статье ZN.UA «Как превратить замороженные российские активы из мертвого капитала в долгосрочный инструмент» пишет соучредительница Международного центра украинской победы и член правления Центра противодействия коррупции Елена Галушка.
description: Она подтвердила дефицит в размере 70 млрд евро и призвала других присоединиться к финансированию.

title: Home Office denies British baby living in Thailand chance to meet great-grandfather in UK
content_c:
The Home Office has denied a great-grandfather from Lancashire the chance of meeting his five-month-old British great-grandson, who lives abroad.
William Cross was born in Thailand on 30 April to parents Matthew Cross, 31, who is from Burnley in Lancashire, and Khin Thant Zin, known as Jue Jue, also 31, a refugee who fled persecution in Myanmar to Thailand.
The family live on the island of Koh Tao, famous for its diving schools and a centre for turtle conservation. It is a popular tourism spot and Cross, a mechanical engineer, opened a steakhouse restaurant there 15 months ago. He met Zin on the island and the couple are now engaged. She works in the restaurant managing social media and human resources.
Cross’s parents have visited the family in Thailand and have met their grandson. But William’s great-grandfather George Kerr, 74, who lives in Clayton-le-Moors in Lancashire, has multiple health problems and so is unable to fly out to Thailand to meet the baby. Instead, a large family gathering was planned in Burnley for Christmas.
Cross said: “My grandfather suffers from ill health and sadly he is unable to travel. He and I have been extremely close all my life and I’m desperate for him to meet his grandchild.”
The family have just signed a lease on a new home and have bought some land on the island for later development.
They assumed that organising a short trip to the UK for a family Christmas would be straightforward. But the Home Office refused Zin’s visitor visa application, which means the family will be unable to travel.
Officials said they were not satisfied she was a “genuine visitor”, and that there was no evidence Zin would return to Thailand because she had not shown evidence of significant family ties there, and she was unable to show sufficient evidence of her income.
“Jue Jue has never had a bank account,” Cross said. “Her brother and sister both live on Koh Tao and her mum is planning to move here when her younger sister has finished school in Myanmar.”
The visitor visa application process is expensive and cumbersome. “They required documentation from my family to be financial guarantors while we’re in the UK. Passport photos of my grandfather, my mum and dad and me, a typed letter from each of us confirming our commitment to sponsorship, a formal letter of invitation from my parents saying they would be comfortable with my partner being in my home,” Cross said.
“We had to travel to Phuket, a journey of two nights and three days from Koh Tao on a ferry and buses, which cost us £400, to complete biometric screening required for the visitor visa application.”
There is no right of appeal against this visa refusal so the couple are preparing a new application, although the Home Office refusal letter warns that future applications are likely to be refused “unless the circumstances of your application change”.
They also need to buy and provide evidence of return flight tickets even though they don’t know whether the new visa application will be granted. They have to make the long journey from the island on ferry and buses a second time to repeat the biometrics.
“By the time we send our next application, the whole thing will have cost us £3,000 with no guarantee of it being accepted,” Cross said.
The family are still hoping that baby William will be able to meet his great-grandfather at Christmas. Temperatures on the island rarely fall below 25C, so back in Burnley his relatives have bought warm baby clothes in the hope he will get a chance to wear them.
A Home Office spokesperson said: “We do not routinely comment on individual cases. All visa applications are carefully considered on their individual merits, in line with the immigration rules and based on the information and evidence provided by the applicant.”

title: Who was Eva Mamlok? Berlin square renamed after Jewish anti-fascist resistance fighter
content_c:
Who was Jewish anti-fascist resistance fighter Eva Mamlok?
October 16, 2026
In the history of German resistance to Nazism, some names have become symbols: Sophie Scholl, Claus von Stauffenberg, Dietrich Bonhoeffer and Georg Elser. Yet many others have remained largely forgotten.
Among them is Eva Mamlok, a young Jewish woman from Berlin whose acts of defiance began in her teenage years and continued until her murder in a Nazi concentration camp.
Now more people will get to know her story as Berlin renames Blücherplatz, a square in the district of Kreuzberg, Eva-Mamlok-Platz on October 16.
"Eva Mamlok was a very remarkable person. As a young Jewish woman from Berlin, her spirit of resistance was particularly striking," said cultural researcher Alexandra Weltz-Rombach, who has worked extensively with the historians' network "Gruppe Eva Mamlok."
'Down with Hitler'
Mamlok was born on May 6, 1918, into a Jewish family in Berlin. They ran a wholesale wine business, and the family belonged to the vibrant Jewish middle class that formed an important part of Berlin's social and economic life during the Weimar Republic.
But Eva came of age just as Germany was descending into dictatorship. When Hitler became chancellor in 1933, she was only 14 years old. She was also a member of the Socialist Workers' Youth (SAJ). Following the suppression of the left-wing political youth organization later that year, she became active in the underground resistance.
According to testimony from Inge Berner (1922-2012), the sole survivor of Mamlok's later resistance group, Eva climbed onto the roof of a department store on Blücherplatz as a teenager and painted the slogan "Down with Hitler."
"She was caught doing that, though she wasn't arrested at that particular moment — that didn't happen until a year later," noted Weltz-Rombach.
Arrested for honoring socialist icons Luxemburg and Liebknecht
Mamlok first appeared in official records in November 1934, after she was arrested for taking part in commemorations for socialist leaders Rosa Luxemburg and Karl Liebknecht at Berlin's Friedrichsfelde Cemetery.
Authorities determined that the 16-year-old held "hostile views toward the state" and placed her in "protective custody until further notice" — a euphemism the regime used to justify imprisonment without trial. She was sent to the women's concentration camp at Moringen in Lower Saxony, where she remained until May 1935.
After her release, she continued her anti-Nazi activities despite the increasing danger, facing persecution both as a political dissident and as a Jew.
In these underground circles, she met Pieter Siemsen (1914–2004), and they remained a couple until he emigrated to Argentina in 1937. The only known surviving photograph of Eva comes from his personal archive.
She had a daughter, Tana, in 1939. The father's identity is unknown, however. The child was placed in a Jewish orphanage in Berlin and deported in 1942 to the Auschwitz-Birkenau extermination camp, where she was murdered.
Meanwhile, because she was Jewish, Mamlok was forced to perform compulsory labor at the Berlin firm F. Butzke Schrauben-Industrie in 1940. There she met other women who shared her opposition to Nazism.
Together they formed what later became known as the "Eva Mamlok Group," an informal resistance network of Jewish and non-Jewish women. They distributed anti-Nazi leaflets and wrote slogans critical of Hitler.
They also shared banned books. "They were books that are today part of Germany's educational canon," from Thomas Mann to Lion Feuchtwanger, said Weltz-Rombach. That the Berlin Central and Regional Library (ZLB), Germany's largest public library, stands on the new Eva-Mamlok-Platz is a fitting symbol of this act of resistance and the importance of books, she added.
Mamlok and others in her group were arrested for distributing this forbidden literature. On January 13, 1942, she was deported from Berlin to the Riga Ghetto in occupied Latvia.
According to Inge Berner's testimony, Mamlok remained active in the resistance there too. For example, she arranged for a contact still in Berlin to send her a cake with a miniature camera hidden inside it to document persecution in the ghetto.
In October 1944, she was sent to the Stutthof Nazi concentration camp, where she died in December of that year.
Replacing old symbols of Franco-German hostility
Blücherplatz was named after the Prussian field marshal Gebhard Leberecht von Blücher, whose most renowned achievement was leading his army against Napoleon at the Battle of Leipzig in 1813 and the Battle of Waterloo in 1815.
Several places, including streets and parks, have been named after him in Germany.
"There is no shortage of Blücher memorial sites," said Weltz-Rombach. "And perhaps it's also time to put an end to this old Franco-German enmity — which is, of course, inherent in the name Blücher, given its Prussian tradition — and to establish, in its place, a different form of remembrance."
The square also happens to be the site of the Carnival of Cultures, a multicultural street festival and parade held every year to celebrate Berlin's global diversity.
Role models for a new generation
Having first heard about Mamlok when a Stolperstein commemorating her was laid in 2011, Weltz-Rombach has been researching her biography for the past few years. The Berlin-based filmmaker, producer and curator has also been sharing the resistance fighter's story through various projects, including an exhibition in 2024 and a podcast series with young Berliners.
Since Mamlok was only a teenager herself when she became politically active, the workshop participants can easily relate to her fate.
These teenagers learn about Mamlok's experiences at the actual locations where she was active, helping them imagine what it would be like to be arrested and imprisoned for six months without trial for doing things that normally wouldn't be considered crimes — such as simply expressing an opinion publicly or laying flowers at a commemorative event, explained Weltz-Rombach.
"Above all, she is, of course, a role model — an example of how one would like to act oneself, and how courageous one would like to be."
"[Women's] resistance was often of a more everyday nature, rather than planting bombs," said Weltz-Rombach. Their stories offer examples of "forms of resistance that have only recently received more attention." Other examples include a 2024 exhibition and the launch of a database dedicated to female resistance fighters.
Even though many of the eyewitnesses are now dead, Weltz-Rombach believes there are still many more of these stories that deserve to be brought into the spotlight: "There are definitely many names we do not know, that are waiting to be further researched."
Edited by: Joshua Lang

title: Drohungen an jüdische Studenten nach AfD-Blockade bei Gedenkfeier
content_c:
AfD-Politiker bei Gedenkfeier Jüdische Studierende werden bedroht
Jüdische Studierende hatten AfD-Politiker Tillschneider daran gehindert, am Gedenken in der Synagoge von Halle teilzunehmen - jetzt bekommen sie Morddrohungen. Die Polizei ermittelt, ob Tillschneider beleidigt wurde.
Vertreter der Jüdischen Studierendenunion Deutschland (JSUD) erhalten nach eigenen Angaben Drohungen, nachdem sie den sachsen-anhaltischen AfD-Politiker Hans-Thomas Tillschneider mit einer Menschenkette den Zutritt zum Gelände der Synagoge in Halle (Saale) verweigert hatten. Vor knapp einer Woche hatte Tillschneider, der Vizepräsident des Landtags ist, am Tag des Gedenkens an den antisemitisch motivierten Anschlag vor sieben Jahren an einer Gedenkfeier teilnehmen wollen.
"Wir bekommen seit der Aktion vor der Synagoge in Halle deutlich mehr Anfeindungen und deutlich mehr Hass - bis hin zu Morddrohungen", sagte der JSUD-Vorsitzende Ron Dekel dem Redaktionsnetzwerk Deutschland (RND). Dekel bezeichnete Tillschneider als "klaren Antisemiten, der von 'Schuldkult' spricht".
"Rechtsextremisten haben in einer Synagoge nichts zu suchen", sagte Dekel weiter. "Es ist statistisch belegt, dass rechtsextremer Antisemitismus, wie wir ihn von der AfD erfahren, die größte Gefahr für jüdisches Leben in Deutschland darstellt", betonte der JSUD-Vorsitzende.
Ermittlung wegen Beleidigung
Die Polizei ermittelt unterdessen wegen des Verdachts der Beleidigung Tillschneiders. Eine unbekannte Zahl von Menschen soll ihn als "Nazi" bezeichnet haben. Das sagte eine Polizeisprecherin. Ob diese der Jüdischen Studierendenunion angehören, könne bislang nicht gesagt werden.
Tillschneider, der Vizepräsident des neuen Landtags in Magdeburg ist, hatte nach der Aktion die Haltung der Studierenden scharf kritisiert und erklärt, er habe sich niemals gegen jüdisches Leben ausgesprochen. Er habe stets betont, "dass es eine jüdisch-deutsche Kultur gibt, die Teil unserer deutschen Kultur ist".
Die AfD Sachsen-Anhalt klagt gegen die Einstufung als "gesichert rechtsextremistische Bestrebung". Das Verfahren ist derzeit ausgesetzt.
Auch Linkspartei "erhebliche Gefahr für jüdisches Leben"
Der Studierendenvertreter äußerte sich auch zur Antisemitismusdebatte rund um die Regierungsbildung in Berlin. Die JSUD habe in den letzten drei Jahren selbst vornehmlich auf den linken Antisemitismus aufmerksam gemacht, der ihnen tagtäglich an den Universitäten begegne.
"Dabei stellt auch die Linkspartei hier in Berlin eine erhebliche Gefahr für jüdisches Leben dar", erklärte Dekel. "Sie ist in Teilen antisemitisch." Er erwarte von den möglichen Koalitionspartnern SPD und Grünen, dass sie dies berücksichtigen.

Die Polizei ermittelt unterdessen wegen des Verdachts der Beleidigung Tillschneiders. Eine unbekannte Zahl von Menschen soll ihn als "Nazi" bezeichnet haben. Das sagte eine Polizeisprecherin. Ob diese der Jüdischen Studierendenunion angehören, könne bislang nicht gesagt werden.
Tillschneider, der Vizepräsident des neuen Landtags in Magdeburg ist, hatte nach der Aktion die Haltung der Studierenden scharf kritisiert und erklärt, er habe sich niemals gegen jüdisches Leben ausgesprochen. Er habe stets betont, "dass es eine jüdisch-deutsche Kultur gibt, die Teil unserer deutschen Kultur ist".
Die AfD Sachsen-Anhalt klagt gegen die Einstufung als "gesichert rechtsextremistische Bestrebung". Das Verfahren ist derzeit ausgesetzt.
Auch Linkspartei "erhebliche Gefahr für jüdisches Leben"
Der Studierendenvertreter äußerte sich auch zur Antisemitismusdebatte rund um die Regierungsbildung in Berlin. Die JSUD habe in den letzten drei Jahren selbst vornehmlich auf den linken Antisemitismus aufmerksam gemacht, der ihnen tagtäglich an den Universitäten begegne.
"Dabei stellt auch die Linkspartei hier in Berlin eine erhebliche Gefahr für jüdisches Leben dar", erklärte Dekel. "Sie ist in Teilen antisemitisch." Er erwarte von den möglichen Koalitionspartnern SPD und Grünen, dass sie dies berücksichtigen.

title: РФ вдарила по обласному центру: пошкоджено будинки, горять автомобілі, є поранені (фото)
content_c:
РФ вдарила по обласному центру: пошкоджено будинки, горять автомобілі, є поранені (фото)
Вибухи і «прильоти» сталися просто серед житлової забудови обласного центру.
На світанку 17 жовтня російські війська атакували житлову забудову Запоріжжя. Є поранені.
Про це повідомив виконувач обов’язків керівника Запорізької обласної військової адміністрації Михайло Семікін.
Унаслідок удару пошкоджено багатоквартирні будинки, також спалахнули автомобілі.
Кількість постраждалих зросла до пʼяти. Серед постраждалих — 22-річна жінка з травмою ока, яку госпіталізували, та 54-річний чоловік, якому надали допомогу на місці. Також поранення дістала 11-річна дівчинка.
ФОТО НАСЛІДКІВ
Нагадаємо, пізно увечері 15 жовтня російські війська також завдали удару по Запоріжжю.Сталось влучання по приватному підприємству, там виникла пожежа.

title: Лукашенко отреагировал на призывы Трампа к смене власти в Украине
content_c:
Президент Беларуси Александр Лукашенко прокомментировал призывы президента США Дональда Трампа к смене руководства в Украине.
Он считает, что этот вопрос не входит в компетенцию американского президента.
Так Лукашенко ответил на вопрос журналистов о том, возможен ли мир в Украине при президентстве Владимира Зеленского, учитывая недавние заявления Трампа.
«Хотите от меня как от политика получить ответ или по существу? Если по существу, то это мое кредо — это не вопрос Трампа. Кто будет в Украине президентом, решит украинский народ», — заявил Лукашенко.
В то же время Лукашенко напомнил, что Зеленский в свое время обещал занимать пост президента только один срок.
«На выборы нужно идти. В этом Трамп прав: обещал — нужно выполнять обещания. Но диктовать не нужно. Трампу не следует указывать Украине, как действовать», — добавил он.
Напомним, 10 октября Трамп заявил, что Владимир Зеленский недостаточно сделал для прекращения войны, и высказал мнение, что Украине нужен другой президент. Американский лидер также обвинил Киев в том, что украинские удары по российским нефтеперерабатывающим заводам способствуют росту цен на дизельное топливо в США. Эти заявления прозвучали на фоне договоренности Вашингтона с Москвой о поставках российского дизельного топлива.
Зеленский ответил, что Украина готова провести выборы, если Россия согласится на 60-дневное прекращение огня. По его словам, такой срок необходим для подготовки и организации голосования.
В то же время 14 октября в интервью журналисту Пирсу Моргану Зеленский заявил, что не собирается уходить в отставку. Он пояснил, что проведение выборов в условиях постоянных российских атак является проблематичным, в частности из-за невозможности гарантировать безопасность избирателей и участие военных, находящихся на фронте.
description: Он напомнил об обещании Зеленского баллотироваться только на один срок.

title: Війська РФ завдали ракетних ударів по двох районах Харкова, є постраждалі – ОВА
content_c:
Російські окупаційні війська в п'ятницю ввечері завдали ракетних ударів по Слобідському та Немишлянському районах Харкова, повідомив начальник Харківської обласної військової адміністрації Олег Синєгубов.
"За попередньою інформацією, ворог наніс ракетний удар по Слобідському району Харкова. Одна людина зазнала гострої реакції на стрес у Слобідському районі. Медики надають всю необхідну допомогу", – написав очільник ОВА в телеграм-каналі.
Згодом Синєгубов поінформував про ще одне ракетне влучання в місті: "Ракетний удар по Немишлянському району. Всі екстрені служби працюють в посиленому режимі".

title: Watch: Did Tesla really just unveil a flying car?
content_c:
Watch: Did Tesla really just unveil a flying car?
A new version of Tesla's Roadster electric sports car, equipped with thrusters which apparently allow it to hover and turn in mid-air, has been unveiled in Texas.
"You're going to see some crazy stuff tonight," the car firm's CEO Elon Musk said as he presented the vehicle at a facility owned by his SpaceX company, which helped develop the model.
Musk said an audience was needed to prove the car "is not AI", before showing a demonstration of the Roadster driving up and off a steep ramp, spinning in the air, and landing using air jets.
But there are several reasons we're unlikely to see a flying car on our roads anytime soon, as the BBC's technology editor Zoe Kleinman explains.

title: Reform councillor resigns after being filmed making racist remarks
content_c:
Alan Feeney has resigned as a Reform councillor for Solihull and Birmingham after backlash over racist comments that were captured in an undercover investigation.
In a Facebook post on Friday, Feeney wrote: “There is no excuse for my comments. With responsibility comes accountability, and it is for that reason that I have resigned every post I hold on both Solihull borough council and Birmingham city council.”
Earlier this week, an ITV investigation revealed secretly recorded footage of Feeney making racist comments about Asian homeowners, calling them “parasites”, and stating that “no more than 1% of [the] British population can be non-white”, during a local election campaign.
Feeney has apologised for his comments. “My remarks were wrong, offensive and completely unacceptable. They do not reflect the standards that the public rightly expects from an elected representative, and I take full responsibility for what I said,” he wrote in a Facebook post.
“The comments do not reflect my true beliefs or opinions, particularly of the communities mentioned in the report. These are communities I have supported countless times in my personal and professional life over many years, many of whom I have been lucky enough to call friends.”
Earlier this year, Feeney won seats in the Shard End ward of Birmingham city council and the Castle Bromwich ward of Solihull metropolitan borough council, and was then appointed deputy mayor of Solihull.
Following the ITV investigation, which is part of a longer series on Reform UK, Feeney announced on Facebook that he was leaving Reform for “personal reasons”, but kept his seats as an independent councillor before resigning.
In a Facebook post, Feeney wrote: “Byelections will be held on a timescale laid out by those councils in the due course. I hope that in time these councils, and the communities they serve can heal and move on.”
Secretly filmed footage showed Feeney making racist remarks alongside two other Reform candidates who went on to become councillors, Jamie Campbell and Chris Whelan, while canvassing during May’s local elections. Both Campbell and Whelan have also resigned after the fallout from the investigation.
Nigel Farage has repeatedly pledged to rid Reform of “extremists” and “bigots”. The party says it carries out vetting checks on everyone who wants to stand for election.
The clips from ITV’s year-long undercover investigation showed Feeney calling Asian homeowners “parasites”, and stating that “no more than 1% of [the] British population can be non-white”.
In a Facebook post Feeney wrote: “I understand that my words have caused hurt and anger, particularly among those from the communities I serve. For that, I am deeply sorry. I will be undertaking intensive personal analysis to understand how these sentiments could have taken root, and ensure they can never do so again.”
Alan Feeney and Reform UK have been approached for comment.

title: EU promotes sovereign, trusted AI as it struggles to catch US and China
content_c:
EU pushes homegrown AI agenda as US, China retain lead
October 16, 2026
If supremacy in artificial intelligence was an Olympic discipline, there would only be two serious contenders for gold on current trajectories: the US and China. The European Union, as has been the case in many areas of cutting-edge technology in recent times, is barely in the AI conversation.
Former European Central Bank President Mario Draghi, whose 2024 report highlighted the EU's desperate need to be more innovative to become more competitive, said recently that AI is "perhaps the most promising" route the EU has to raise growth today. However, he decried the fact that the European Union controls little of the value chain.
"Being cut off from AI, once the economy runs on it, would be more like being cut off from the US financial system," he wrote in an opinion piece for the Financial Times. "The effects would be catastrophic."
Draghi's spirit was on full display in Dublin on Wednesday at an international AI summit the Irish government convened as part of its six-month stint hosting the rotating EU presidency.
The summit's motto, "Harnessing AI to Revolutionize Europe's Competitiveness," might as well have been dreamed up by the Italian former prime minister.
AI safety concerns shadow growth agenda
Harnessing AI has become a lot more complicated. A slew of controversies around AI agents going rogue, from the Hugging Face attack in June when 1,200 agents hacked an online platform, to an Anthropic-designed agent sending a fake tip to US police over an unsolved murder, have caused alarm.
Many from within the tech industry, including Microsoft founder Bill Gates and the leading AI frontier labs themselves, have called for a development pausein order for safety measures to catch up.
Yet positivity was largely the name of the game at the summit, with tech and AI industry leaders joining Irish and EU politicians to declare AI's transformative economic and societal potential — while also emphasizing the need for strong regulation and safety standards.
Irish Prime Minister Micheal Martin made it clear that Ireland was all in on AI. He echoed European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen's recent assertion that the technology represented a "tipping point." He also repeatedly highlighted what he sees as the bloc's commitment to safety.
"We are determined to capture the dividend by mitigating the risks," Martin told the event. "In Europe, we have charted our path ... balancing innovation and opportunity with a trustworthy, human-centered approach to AI."
AI critics say key concerns overlooked
Meanwhile, Henna Virkkunen, the European Commission executive vice-president for tech sovereignty, security and democracy, revealed at the event that the EU had begun its first enforcement actions under its new AI Act, requesting information around security and safety from advanced AI model providers.
However, other topics that concern AI's many critics, from those fearing the massive environmental impact of data centers to others warning about possible AI-related job losses, were largely absent from the discussions.
Outside the venue, a group of protesters led by People Before Profit, a left-wing Irish political party, criticized the summit for not focusing on these issues.
"There is a deliberate blurring of the line here with the type of AI that is being promoted," Alexandra Day, one of the protest organizers, told DW.
"It is really being pushed on workers with very little consent. There's no right for workers to opt out of using AI now that it's coming into the workplace."
Europe faces a widening AI gap
A sense of urgency was palpable from the speakers inside the summit. Executives from some of the world's biggest AI and tech firms talked up Europe's potential. Yet the EU evidently has plenty of ground to catch up on in terms of AI development.
Despite ramping up its data center capacity, it still lags far behind the US and China. It hosts 5% of the world's AI computing capacity compared to around 75% for the US.
The EU is conspicuously absent from lists of the leading AI frontier labs, with only French company Mistral coming close to rivaling the top labs. Its production of leading-edge chips is also nowhere near that of the top US or Taiwanese producers.
As part of its plan to make ground on the US and China, the Irish government, in its role as EU presidency host, presented a policy document at the event.
The so-called "Dublin Declaration" outlines political commitments to strengthen Europe's AI capabilities, including infrastructure investment and financial backing for European AI companies.
In keeping with Draghi's calls for Europe to develop its own AI sovereignty, particularly in supply chains and infrastructure, the declaration suggests that European firms reliant on non-EU cloud and computing services may face additional compliance pressures.
Can Europe balance innovation and regulation?
However, not everyone is convinced by the EU's capacity to either ramp up AI capacity or develop effective regulation.
Eddie Wilson, CEO of European airline Ryanair, said he doubted Brussels could regulate AI well without stifling innovation.
"The last thing you want is people regulating this industry who don't know anything about it," he told DW. "That's generally what happens in Brussels."
Ryanair recently made a major deal with Google to use its cloud data system and its AI platform Gemini Enterprise. It's precisely the kind of collaboration with US AI supply chains that the EU says it wants companies to move away from.
"I worry for Europe because these tech companies need to move at speed," said Wilson. He believes the environment in the US is more amenable to innovation.
"If they're not going to do it here, they're going to do it elsewhere. They're going to do it in China and they're going to do it in the US."
Edited by: Tim Rooks
description: At an international AI summit in Dublin, EU leaders promoted trusted and independent artificial intelligence. Critics question whether the bloc can close the gap with the US and China while maintaining strict regulation.
